explanation: Mark reachable prefix lengths, starting with zero. From each reachable position, advance by every dictionary word that matches there. The final position is reachable exactly when segmentation is possible.
timeComplexity: O((n + 1) times (D + 1)) time for string length n and total dictionary characters D, including an empty dictionary. For each reachable position, comparison with all words costs at most their total length D; even unreachable positions require the outer O(n) scan.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. The reachable-prefix table has n+1 booleans; comparisons do not store new substrings.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Reachable[i] means the prefix ending before i can be segmented into dictionary words. From any reachable i, appending a matching word produces another valid segmented prefix. Conversely, every nonempty valid segmentation has a final dictionary word appended after a reachable earlier prefix, so these transitions discover every valid endpoint.
walkthrough: For "sunflower" and dictionary ["sun","flow","flower"], mark prefix length 3 after matching sun. From that position flower reaches the full string length 9. Therefore "sun"+"flower" is a valid segmentation and the result is true.
edgeCases: The full string must be covered, not merely a prefix.
